children: What happened?

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after AI-linked shares continued to pull back. Anthropic slid more than 10% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom.

Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported. Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth.

Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Zooming in on nLIGHT

nLIGHT’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 69 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for nLIGHT and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock dropped 5.7% on the news that the Commerce Department's move to close third-country loopholes for Chinese AI compute leasing added export-policy risk to optical and interconnect suppliers already navigating Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation ahead of Nvidia's earnings announcement.

Nvidia has directly funded the data-center shift from copper wiring to silicon photonics, investing $2 billion each in Coherent and Lumentum, which Marvell Technology agreed to buy in an all-stock deal, alongside multi-year purchase commitments, CNBC noted. Reuters added that Nvidia took an equity stake and made multi-billion-dollar plant prepayments to Corning for optical glass. With Nvidia's photonics-centric Feynman GPU architecture slated for 2028, per CNBC, UBS and Mizuho cutting Nvidia price targets ahead of the earnings announcement kept roadmap continuity and overseas cluster demand under scrutiny.

Optical and interconnect suppliers commit factory capacity years ahead of deployment around Nvidia's hardware schedule. When third-country compute curbs cloud international cluster expansion alongside leadership turnover that obscures post-2027 priorities, component makers backed by bespoke prepayments trade as proxies for contract durability.

nLIGHT is down 15.3% since the beginning of the year, and at $32.48 per share, it is trading 61.8% below its 52-week high of $84.95 from May 2026. Despite the year-to-date decline, investors who bought $1,000 worth of nLIGHT’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,199.
